A security conscious user can currently allowlist explicit commands (with no wildcards) to prevent this sort of injection. This change would significantly weaken those safeguards

This did it for me (for claude code usage)
```
# Let tmux recognize Shift+Enter from iTerm2, then forward as CSI u bytes
set -s extended-keys on
set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'
bind -n S-Enter send-keys -H 1b 5b 31 33 3b 32 75
```

I can confirm that tool calls sometimes also consume premium requests, for example. At least, that is my assumption at present. Here are the steps I used to verify the increased usage: First picture (left most) is pre opencode execution. I had 40% used of my free quota. Used the free tier, because of the open issues with the copilot integration. (Which includes 50 premium request, so 1 premium request equals 2%). In the second most left picture we see the quota after the opencode execution with 5 tool calls (in this case 5x echo something through powershell). As one can see the quota goes from 40% to 46%, which represents the usage of 3 premium requests for on single prompt with 5 tool calls. Third is after the copilot cli execution with the same prompt for 5 powershell echo tool calls, nothing else. This correctly used one premium requests. Last picture is for verification that is was really just one premium request. Opencode version used was 1.2.5
Fixed in #11840 by @neriousy — prompt input styling was adjusted to handle long model names and align right-hand icons properly, resolving the overflow on narrow viewports.

Fixed in #13973 by @nexxeln — SSE transport was hardened with anti-buffering headers, 10s heartbeats, client heartbeat timeout (15s), and visibility-based reconnect. `server.connected` is now treated as a refresh trigger, re-bootstrapping active directories after reconnect to reconcile missed events. No more stale UI or history rollback after backgrounding.

Ripgrep respects gitignore by default and that's intentional. We are prolly moving off ripgrep soon but in the meantime u can just make a .ignore or a .rgignore and override the gitignore rule for ripgrep. 

Ex:
```
# .gitignore
.github/work/

# .rgignore (or .ignore)
!.github/work/
```

I dont think this is quite accurate. Did you read what is considered a task in that file? It's only compaction or subtask invocations. A subtask invocation only occurs from manual slash command invocation that specifies a subagent or is instructed to run as a subtask.

In both cases we want these to occur in order.

The llm can call the task tool multiple times at once and those will all be evaluated in parallel. you can test this easily by editing the task tool to sleep for like 30 seconds if the agent is a particular one then have any model that can call parallel tools and tell it to call 3 agents at once. 

You will see the other agents complete before the sleep one, even if sleep one is called first.
